LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 9.1.2 SPEAKING FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1: Listening and Speaking 9.1.2 Speaking Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 9.1.2 Speaking Fluency, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can we make our oral presentations effective? 2. Why is it important to accurately pronounce sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. differentiate the consonant sounds / ð / and/ θ / in oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.2 Speaking Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate intonation in different types of sentences in oral presentations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.2 Speaking Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse aspects of fluency in an informative skit,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.2 Speaking Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 9.1.2 Speaking Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
The learner makes critical observations as they collaborate with others to analyse the recorded or live skit on aspects of

fluency namely accuracy, speed and expressiveness.

Values:
107

Integrity: The learner exhibits self-discipline while creating and performing a skit on the theme featuring the target sounds and

different aspects of fluency and recording it.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learners support programmes: The learner is assisted to identify and nurture their gifts and talents as they perform the skit.
